Server slice of workspace feature **013-matrix-media-file-service** — conversation message attachments, working from both the Alkemio web client and a native Element/Matrix client, with every file stored once through file-service and governed by chat membership.

> ⚠️ **Not mergeable yet** — see "Blocked on" at the bottom. Opening now for review.

## What this adds

- **Per-conversation storage bucket + authorization.** Resolves the existing "no storage for conversations" gap. Credential-based: the policy grants READ to holders of the conversation-member credential, so access tracks membership live rather than an enumerated list. Created eagerly on conversation create, with a backfill migration for pre-existing conversations.
- **`Message.attachments`** — read resolution to an Alkemio document URL, so the web client never needs Matrix credentials.
- **Inbound re-home.** Media arriving from Element is staged by the Synapse provider into a reserved `matrix_media` bucket, then MOVEd into the conversation's bucket on `message.received`, with a policy minted and `createdBy` set to the sending member. COPY (not MOVE) on re-share into a second conversation.
- **Outbound send path** — attachment validation (≤10, ownership, single-use), display-name sanitization, and staged-media cleanup after 24h.
- **`externalReference` migration.** The prod `file`-table schema is owned by server's TypeORM (the `server-migration` cron), not by file-service — file-service does runtime CRUD only.

Gated end-to-end by **`communications.message_attachments.enabled`** (env `COMMUNICATIONS_MESSAGE_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED`), default **off**. The flag gates the send path, the read paths, the cleanup sweep, **and** the eager per-conversation provisioning — so this ships inert.

## Boundaries worth reviewing

The client + server + adapter tier is a Synapse **client**, not a replacement. Consequences that are deliberate, not gaps:

- **No delete-release, no media GC, no cross-side reference counting.** Deleting a message is a per-event redaction, exactly as in Element; blob reclamation is Synapse's (retention/purge).
- **No image-dimension measurement.** Declared `info.w`/`info.h` are used as-is, as every Matrix client does. Outbound sends still populate them.
- **Alkemio's media policy constrains what Alkemio accepts, never what Synapse accepts.** The reserved `matrix_media` staging bucket is unrestricted (no MIME allow-list, no size cap) — enforcing Alkemio policy at the storage provider would turn a tiered client into a homeserver-wide upload restriction, in every room, including rooms Alkemio does not own.
- **A multi-attachment send is 1 + N independent Matrix events and is not atomic**, matching Element.

Two read-path calls (`getDocumentMeta`, `pinDocumentDurableBestEffort`) deliberately **bypass the shared file-service circuit breaker**: direct request, short timeout, zero retries, every failure degrading to null/false. An unpaginated read must not be able to trip the breaker that guards uploads platform-wide.

## Merging `develop` caught a regression in this feature

`develop`'s bucket authorization cascade skips documents on `!document.tagset`. Inbound Element attachments are tagset-less but **do** carry their own policy, so they were skipped entirely and never re-inherited on a membership change — **a member who left a conversation kept READ on its inbound attachments.** Re-keyed to `!document.authorization`, which is `develop`'s own stated discriminator (its comment says snapshots are "NULL-authz"; its test is named *"skips policy-less internal files during the authorization cascade"* with an `authorization: undefined` fixture). All of `develop`'s tests still pass, plus ours.

## Testing

- **9748 passing / 28 skipped / 0 failing.**
- Biome exit 0. `schema.graphql` regenerates byte-identical.
- No migration drift against a live Postgres.

## Blocked on

`@alkemio/matrix-adapter-lib` is pinned to a **pkg.pr.new preview** (matrix-adapter#67). `tsc` currently reports 11 errors purely from that pin — the preview carries the attachment DTOs but not `develop`'s newer hierarchy DTOs (`COMMUNICATION_HIERARCHY_SET_CHILDREN`), and `0.8.19` carries the reverse. The two are **disjoint, not ordered**. A local type shim would be actively wrong: the hierarchy constant is missing from the preview's runtime `.js`, so faking the type would make hierarchy reconcile publish to routing key `undefined`.

Unblocking sequence: **matrix-adapter#67 merges → tag → `@alkemio/matrix-adapter-lib` publishes to npm → this PR repins to that version.** `develop`'s new `.scripts/check-vendor-lib-pins.sh` enforces this mechanically (it fails any `pkg.pr.new` specifier), so the repin is a hard merge gate, not a nicety.

## What & why

Adds an optional **`sendNotification`** flag to `CreateContributionOnCalloutInput` so a contributor can add a response or a task without notifying the whole Space. Closes the server half of `alkem-io/notifications#593`.

Two changes:

1. **One additive nullable input field**, `sendNotification: Boolean = true`, on the mutation subclass `CreateContributionOnCalloutInput` — deliberately **not** on `CreateCalloutContributionInput`, which doubles as the `CreateCalloutContributionData` template/replay surface and already carries a callout-level flag.
2. **The five duplicated per-contribution-type notification emissions are hoisted** out of `processActivity{Post,Link,Whiteboard,Memo,CollaboraDocument}Created` into **one gated call** in `createContributionOnCallout`.

## Load-bearing design decisions

- **The wire default stays `true`.** "Off by default" (AC2) lives in client form state, not the contract. A contract default of `false` would have silently inverted behaviour for every non-client producer — the `createPostOnCallout` test helper alone has ~68–104 call sites that pass no flag.
- **The gate is `sendNotification !== false`** — explicit-false only, never truthiness — so an in-process/MCP producer that omits the field still notifies.
- **AC4 is structural, not test-enforced.** The emission is dispatched *after* the activity/analytics blocks with `.catch()`, so a notification failure can never drop the activity row or fail the mutation. A silenced contribution still appears in activity feeds.
- **One flag suppresses both channels** (`SPACE_COLLABORATION_CALLOUT_CONTRIBUTION` *and* `SPACE_ADMIN_COLLABORATION_CALLOUT_CONTRIBUTION`), honouring AC3 literally — see the tracked residual below.
- The flag is **reduce-only**: nested inside the pre-existing `visibility === PUBLISHED` and `calloutsSet.type === COLLABORATION` guards, so it can never force an emission the platform would otherwise withhold.

No DDL, no migration, no new `NotificationEvent`, no `@alkemio/notifications-lib` bump, no config key or env var. The wire to the notifications service is byte-identical.

## Evidence

Built with `/forge`: model-blind architect council (3 contrarian seats, 15 objections, 24 agreed questions, 3 contested forks) → Fable chief synthesis → implementation → live verification → adversarial review.

**Live verification** against a running stack:
- Emission-layer A/B: switch **ON** publishes both events; **OFF** publishes neither.
- Wire-default pin proven live: omitting the field delivers mail exactly as before (MailSlurper 86→96, recipients including a distinct space admin).
- AC4 proven live: suppressed contributions still appear in the callout and activity feed.
- Unit `callout.resolver.mutations.spec.ts` **75/75**; `post-contribution.it-spec.ts` **9/9**; gql-live all 6 feature scenarios; acceptance US1 6/6, US2 3/3, US3 3/4.

**Review**: 3 rounds, 73 findings raised → 10 confirmed, 9 fixed. Security verdict for this repo: **conditional** — no critical or high findings open; authorization unchanged (`CONTRIBUTE` still enforced before any work); no secrets, dependency, migration, raw SQL, or outbound-call changes.

One review finding worth calling out, because it defeated the whole feature's observability: the suppression record was emitted at `verbose`, but production runs `SERVER_LOGGING_LEVEL: "warn"` — so **in production nothing would have been written at all**. Now `logger.warn`, with the level pinned in the spec so it cannot silently regress.

## Tracked residuals (not blockers, deliberately recorded)

- **R-1 (medium, security)** — any actor holding `CONTRIBUTE` can suppress the **space-admin** notification about their own contribution, placing a moderation/detection signal under the control of the contributor whose content it announces. This is deliberate, human-ruled behaviour (intake ruling D-OP2 over the architect council's recorded dissent D1). Compensating controls: the activity feed still records every suppressed contribution, space admins retain an independent per-recipient opt-out, every suppression writes a structured `warn` record, and inline/DRAFT/moved contribution paths were already silent beforehand. **Residual-risk acceptance is a human release-gate decision.**
- **R-2 (high, tracked)** — ships with **no runtime kill switch** (intake ruling, dissent D2). Rollback is a code revert and **must be client-first**: reverting the server while a deployed client still sends the field would make every response/task creation fail GraphQL validation.
- 3 low server hardening/drift items.

Adds a nullable `CollaboraDocument.previewUrl` field so clients can render a
thumbnail of a saved Collabora document without opening the editor.
`workspace#059-collabora-preview-streaming`.

## What this does

`previewUrl` resolves the existing internal backing `Document` relation and
returns the same-origin authorized path built from its stable `fileID`:

```
/api/private/wopi/files/{fileID}/preview
```

It returns `null` when no backing file exists, which is why the field is
nullable — a legacy or orphaned `CollaboraDocument` can lack the relation.

Deliberate properties:

- **The backing `Document` is never exposed** through GraphQL, and no WOPI
  editor token is issued. Only the stable `fileID` crosses the boundary, per
  ADR `0012`.
- **The URL is not a bearer credential.** Normal `CollaboraDocument` field
  authorization applies here, and the WOPI endpoint independently re-authorizes
  every byte request against the source document's current policy.
- **`/wopi-private/...` is an internal router path** — never returned to
  GraphQL, never constructed by the client. The gateway rewrites the public
  path onto it.
- The `fileID` is URL-encoded.

## Schema impact

Additive only: one nullable field, **zero breaking changes** per `schema:diff`.
Existing `CollaboraDocument` field authorization is unchanged.

## Tests

Resolver and service unit tests cover a present backing file, a missing relation
resolving to `null`, stable-`fileID` URL encoding, and that existing field
authorization still gates the field. Verified live against a booted stack via
GraphQL probes, including an introspection check that the field is a nullable
`String` and that no `Document`-typed field was added to `CollaboraDocument`.

## Known follow-up

`previewUrl` performs a per-document `findOne` with the `document` relation, and
there is no `CollaboraDocument` dataloader in `src/core/dataloader`, so a
callouts list selecting the field issues one backing-document query per item.
Raised in review and tracked as a follow-up rather than fixed here: the loader
belongs alongside the existing dataloader creators and should batch the
`document` relation for the list path generally, not only for `previewUrl`.
It is a performance regression on an existing list surface, not a correctness
defect — flagging for the maintainers' call on whether it blocks merge.

## Ordering

This field can deploy before anything consumes it, but it must not be relied on
until the WOPI endpoint and its gateway route are reachable in the target
environment. See the rollout ordering in the workspace spec's `plan.md`.

## Spec

`agents-hq/specs/059-collabora-preview-streaming/` —
`contracts/graphql-preview-url.md`, `tasks/server.md`.

Related (remain open until manually closed): alkem-io/server#4970, alkem-io/client-web#9353.

Workspace spec: `workspace#063-callout-transfer-flow-state` — https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/feat/063-callout-transfer-flow-state/specs/063-callout-transfer-flow-state/

## What was still broken after #6339

QA re-tested #6021 after #6339 merged and acceptance criterion 3 ("same logic applies when the destination's innovation flow was changed via template", the alkem-io/client-web#9353 sequence) still failed: the transferred callout is tagged with one of the destination's **old** state names and shows on no flow tab.

## Root cause (proven at code level)

The transfer logic from #6339 is correct but validates against the destination's flow-state `TagsetTemplate` (`allowedValues` / `defaultSelectedValue`), and that template drifts from the `InnovationFlow`'s actual states through three writers:

1. **Template apply** — `updateCollaborationFromSpaceTemplate` loads the target collaboration with `calloutsSet.tagsetTemplateSet` (eager `tagsetTemplates`, `cascade: true` on every hop). `updateInnovationFlowStates` updates a *separately loaded* copy of the template and saves it; the applier's final `collaborationService.save(targetCollaboration)` then cascades the **stale** in-memory template back over the row, reverting `allowedValues`/`defaultSelectedValue` to the pre-template names. The destination's own callouts stay visible (they are re-homed by state *name*), which is why only transfers exposed it.
2. **Add / delete a single state** — neither `createStateOnInnovationFlow` nor `deleteStateOnInnovationFlow` ever rewrote the template.
3. **Rename** — `TagsetService.updateTagsetsSelectedValue` re-tagged callouts in memory on the rename branch and `continue`d without `save`; nothing cascades to those tagsets, so callouts in a renamed phase kept the old name on reload.

## Fix (behaviour-only; no DDL, no GraphQL change)

- `TemplateApplierService`: re-read the callouts set's `TagsetTemplateSet` after the flow-state update, so the cascade save persists the current vocabulary and template-added callouts are classified against it.
- `InnovationFlowService`: add/delete state rewrite the flow-state template; one shared default rule (`resolveDefaultFlowStateName`: current state while it exists, else first) now backs template apply, rename, add and delete.
- `TagsetService`: persist the re-tag on the rename branch.
- Migration `1789000000000-ResyncFlowStateTagsetTemplates` (data-only, idempotent, no-op `down`): re-derives `allowedValues` from the flow's states in flow order, repairs a missing/unknown default, and moves callout flow-state tags that match no state (case-insensitively) to that default. Existing drifted spaces (acceptance, where QA reproduced this) are healed on deploy.

## Regression tests (each RED on `develop`, GREEN here)

- `template.applier.service.spec.ts` — the #9353 sequence: the graph handed to the cascade save carries the template's new state names; template-added callouts see the updated vocabulary.
- `innovation.flow.service.spec.ts` — add-state (incl. sort-order insertion) and delete-state (incl. deleting the current state) rewrite the vocabulary with the shared default rule; two pins for the default rule on the template path.
- `tagset.service.spec.ts` — rename branch saves the re-tagged tagset.
- `src/migrations/__tests__/1789000000000-ResyncFlowStateTagsetTemplates.spec.ts` — structural pins (three ordered UPDATEs, idempotence guards, case-insensitive re-tag, no DDL, no-op down).
- #6339's transfer pins (`classification.service.spec.ts`, `callout.transfer.service.spec.ts`) unchanged and green.

| before | `Stale A,Stale B` | `Stale A` | 7 |
| after first run | `Home` (= the flow's states) | `Home` | 0 |
| second run | `UPDATE 0` / `UPDATE 0` / `UPDATE 0` | | |

## Root cause

Memo signing renders the live Yjs projection and resolves every internal image through document metadata and file-service bytes. Existing memos can still reference a document whose metadata row is absent, or whose metadata exists while the backing bytes return a typed 404. The renderer correctly fails rather than silently changing the signed output, but the existing collaboration migration worker had no memo-image discovery or repair path.

## Fix

- extends the existing one-shot collaboration migration worker with `--repair-memo-images --actor-id <uuid>`; it is a read-only dry run by default, and mutation requires explicit `--apply`
- reads each current memo through the live collaboration room, reports exact missing references and repeated occurrence counts, and only treats typed metadata absence or a typed file-service 404 as confirmed loss
- leaves authorization failures, transport failures/timeouts, 5xx responses, malformed responses, foreign-bucket metadata, and malformed internal locators untouched and reports the memo as failed
- removes only confirmed-missing image nodes from the fresh live Yjs document and persists via the existing correlated durability-barrier path, so concurrent edits are not overwritten by a stale snapshot
- preserves valid/external images and unrelated memo text, formatting, lists, and tables; rerunning a completed repair is a no-op
- reports visual loss explicitly, while the repaired projection is also the projection used by preview/signing

The memo image schema contains no alternate byte source to recover a genuinely absent internal document. Images whose metadata and non-empty file-service bytes are available are preserved.

## What / why

A persona on the **generic** engine had no server-side route to receive a stored prompt graph: the invocation builder attached `promptGraph` only inside the `EXPERT` branch. So the declarative graph support merged in [virtual-contributor#122](https://github.com/alkem-io/virtual-contributor/pull/122) (conditional edges, retrieve/echo nodes, the shipped workshop payload) was live but **unreachable through configuration**.

This adds a `PROMPT_GRAPH_ENGINES` allowlist covering `expert` + `generic-openai`, new GraphQL authoring fields for the node/edge forms, an activation guide, and the workshop authoring fixture.

Closes #6385. Spec: `workspace#053-generic-prompt-graph`.

Most of the diff is tests and docs, but **three source files change existing behaviour** — worth reading rather than skimming:

**`ai.persona.resolver.mutations.ts` — the `aiServerUpdateAiPersona` body was restructured, not extended.** The fetch and the authorization check moved inside a `try`, an audit call was added on both the success and failure paths, and a constructor dependency was added. **The authorization check is unchanged in substance and still runs before any update**: same `grantAccessOrFail`, same `AuthorizationPrivilege.UPDATE`, same policy object, same position relative to the mutation — only its enclosing block moved. The server's wire default stays `true`; "off by default" (AC2) is client form state. Putting `false` in the contract would have silently inverted behaviour for every non-client API producer. The client sends an explicit `false` only when the user leaves the switch off.

## Summary

The streaming I/O this service depends on was upstreamed in [davidbyttow/govips#539](https://github.com/davidbyttow/govips/pull/539) — which landed our [#530](https://github.com/davidbyttow/govips/pull/530) with authorship preserved — plus follow-up [#540](https://github.com/davidbyttow/govips/pull/540). The `replace` directive pointing at `antst/govips` is no longer needed.

```diff
- github.com/davidbyttow/govips/v2 v2.18.0
+ github.com/davidbyttow/govips/v2 v2.18.1-0.20260808163446-115936532956
-
- replace github.com/davidbyttow/govips/v2 => github.com/antst/govips/v2 v2.0.0-20260612014756-be0d7643869e
```

## Why this is safe

Upstream is a **strict superset** of the pinned fork commit (`be0d764`):

- **Exported API diff is empty.** Every exported declaration in the fork's `vips` package exists upstream with unchanged signatures — including all seven symbols this service uses (`LoadImageFromReader`, `SetStreamDiscThreshold`, `SetStreamScratchDir`, `SetPipeReadLimit`, plus stock APIs).
- **Line-level:** every non-comment line the fork added to `vips/*.{go,c,h}` is either verbatim upstream or accounted for by upstream's refactor of the inline export-param mapping into shared `*ParamsFromExport` helpers. `transcode.go` is byte-identical; `govips.go` identical; `image.go` differs only by a doc comment.
- **The only fork-side deletion is dead code:** `save_tiff_to_target` in `stream.c`. Both versions take the buffered early-return path for TIFF (libtiff requires seekable output), so it was never called.

## What we gain

Two real robustness fixes on our streaming path:

- `sourceRead` **bounds retries on a pathological `(0, nil)` reader** — the fork's unbounded `for {}` can spin forever inside a cgo callback, pinning a libvips worker thread.
- `takeErr` now actually **clears** the error it takes, so a stale error can't resurface on a later call.

Plus sub-format sniffing for streamed AVIF/BMP/PSD (#540 — relevant to 019 if we ever read `Format()` on the streaming path), typed `SaveToWriterJpeg/Png/Webp/Tiff/Heif/Gif` variants, BigTIFF detection, WebP `TargetSize` version guard, greyscale background fix.

## Caveat

Streaming is **not yet in a tagged release** — `v2.18.0` (2026-04-01) predates the merge and there's been no tag since. This pins an upstream master pseudo-version. Still strictly better than the fork: no `replace`, so Renovate can now see and bump it. Move to `v2.19.0` once tagged.

`go mod tidy` also pruned `go.sum` entries that only existed to satisfy the fork's own `go.mod` (chi 5.3.0, nats-server 2.14.2, older `x/crypto`/`x/net`/`x/sync`/`x/sys`/`x/text`) — pure removals, no `require` version changed.

## Docs

`CLAUDE.md` and `internal/imaging/testdata/README.md` updated. `specs/020-stream-uploads/{research,plan,spec}.md` got dated supersede notes at the three points that prescribed the `replace` directive — spec bodies left intact as point-in-time records. `README.md` needed no change (mentions govips, never the fork).

| `go test -tags vips ./...` | 12/12 packages ok |

## What & why

Cross-service coverage for the contribution notify switch (`alkem-io/notifications#593`) — the API-level pins plus one persisted acceptance walk.

## What's here

**`post-contribution.it-spec.ts` — four appended cases** (`+162` lines, **zero deletions**; the six pre-existing cases are byte-identical):

| case | pins |
|---|---|
| `sendNotification: false` suppresses the member **and** the admin notification | the AC3-literal ruling (D-OP2), so it is deliberate behaviour and not drift |
| `sendNotification: true` notifies exactly as today | same recipients and content as the omitted-flag path |
| **omitting** `sendNotification` still notifies everyone | the wire default stays notify — the regression this feature could most plausibly cause |
| the activity log entry is written even though `sendNotification` is false | AC4 |

Plus a regenerated lib GraphQL client, a flag-aware `createPostOnCalloutWithNotification` helper (the legacy `createPostOnCallout` is left **untouched** so its ~68–104 call sites keep omitting the field), and a persisted Playwright walk `client-web/tests/contribution-notify-switch.spec.ts` covering US1-AS1…AS5.

**Extend-never-edit is mechanically verifiable**: the diff against the branch point is insertions only for the pre-existing specs.

Status: `post-contribution.it-spec.ts` runs **9/9 green** against a live stack (5 pre-existing + 4 new).

## Four defects this slice had, and what they teach

These were caught by live verification and adversarial review, and are worth reading as review notes rather than trivia — three of the four were tests that *looked* green while asserting nothing:

1. **Two collection-time dereferences.** The describe block read `baseScenario` (and later `TestUserManager.users`) at describe scope, before `beforeAll` populates them. The file threw during collection, so **zero** tests ran — taking the pre-existing cases down with it. A green suite summary elsewhere hid it.
2. **A vacuous pin.** The new describe is a *sibling* of `Notifications - post`, so it never inherited that block's `enablePostNotifications` — and the preceding test deliberately **disables** notifications for every role. The suppression case therefore passed even though it could not fail: with notifications off for everyone, "no mail arrived" proves nothing. Fixed by mirroring the enable list in the describe's own `beforeAll`.
3. **Shared-state leak.** An earlier fix re-enabled notifications for eight globally-seeded personas without restoring them, flipping the state handed to the rest of the serial run and breaking an untouched neighbouring spec. Not visible in a single-file re-run.
4. **Ungated queue assertions.** The acceptance walk asserted through the RabbitMQ management API without the repo's `rabbitMqManagementConfigured()` guard, while the nightly workflow sets no `RABBITMQ_MANAGEMENT_*` — so its emission checks would have gone green when the queue simply did not exist.

Related, worth knowing when running the notification suites locally: these specs share one MailSlurper mailbox and clobber each other's counts when run in parallel — `community-updates.it-spec.ts` passes 5/5 alone but fails in the directory sweep. Run spec **files** one at a time.

## Security note — please read

The persisted walk signs in through the Kratos **UI**, so `AUTH_TEST_HARNESS_PASSWORD` is typed into the page. The nightly config sets `retries: 2` with `trace: 'on-all-retries'` and `video: 'retain-on-failure'`, and `scripts/publish-report.sh` pushes report attachments — **`data/**` included** — to the `gh-pages` branch of this **public** repo. Any flake would therefore publish that plaintext credential to the public site.

This PR adds `use: { trace: 'off', video: 'off' }` to the new nightly project, so **this walk cannot contribute a copy**.

**It does not fix the underlying channel.** The publishing path predates this feature and, per the security review, the exposure is already realised by an existing sibling walk. Three actions remain **open and are not addressed here**: rotating `AUTH_TEST_HARNESS_PASSWORD`, purging `playwright/**/data/**` from `gh-pages` history, and stripping attachments before publishing (or making the Pages site private). Raising these with the repo owners is recommended independently of this PR.

- Spec / plan / evidence ledger: `agents-hq/specs/070-contribution-notify-switch/`

Durable Playwright cover for **workspace#051-cleverbase-account-linking** — the Connected Accounts section on Security settings, shipped in alkem-io/client-web#10176 (merged to `develop` 2026-08-24).

The forge run's Phase-V acceptance walks were driven ad-hoc and **persisted no specs** — its own ledger recorded *"Emitted @forge-acceptance specs: none persisted … the durable-spec follow-up can ride the test-suites flow."* This is that follow-up.

## Coverage — 13 cases, 7 files

`client-web/src/functional-e2e/connected-accounts/`

| Case | What it pins |
|---|---|
| CA-01 | three provider rows *Not connected* + Connect, read-only credential rows, no identity leakage |
| CA-02 | credential rows route via in-page anchors to the password/passkey cards, no inline mutation |
| CA-05 | a password error stays inside the password card (does not echo into the section) |
| CA-06 | owner-only: a platform admin on another user's security URL is redirected, no settings flow created |
| CA-04 | fail-closed when the settings flow is unreadable — explicit error + retry, **zero** provider rows; retry recovers in place |
| CA-03 / CA-07 | last-method lock shows a focusable `aria-disabled` Disconnect carrying its reason; curing the lock flips the same row to enabled |
| CA-30 / CA-31 | disconnect requires the confirm dialog — confirming POSTs `unlink=<provider>` with zero provider contact, Cancel fires no POST |
| CA-20 / CA-21 | Connect natively POSTs `link=<provider>` + CSRF to the flow action and writes the outcome marker; returning from an interrupted Connect announces the retry notice once |
| CA-40 / CA-42 / CA-43 / CA-43b | errored-flow resume (`4000007`) on bare `/settings`, and each outcome announcement — pending, connected, disconnected — exactly once |
| CA-41 | regression: the recovery-born settings flow still renders *Set new password* on bare `/settings` (the T027 resume seam) |

Live dev stack throughout; Kratos settings-flow **reads** are mocked only where a state cannot be provoked deterministically (locked rows, unreadable flow, completed round-trips). All URLs resolve at runtime from each persona's own profile URL — never a hardcoded `/user/<slug>`.

## Harness changes these depend on

- **`authenticated-session.fixture.ts`** — persona sessions are validated against Kratos `whoami` before reuse, and gain `maxSessionAgeSeconds`. Kratos gates privileged self-service operations behind `privileged_session_max_age` (15m); a live-but-stale cached session makes a privileged submit redirect to a re-auth screen instead of returning the expected settings-flow response. Specs doing privileged work now re-mint rather than mis-assert.
- **`config/global-setup.ts`** — provision personas through the Kratos **admin** API when `KRATOS_ADMIN_URL` is reachable (deterministic; no HIBP/self-service policy; a reset Kratos store heals on the next run instead of timing out every login), falling back to self-service registration otherwise. Then warm every persona's storage state **serially, before any worker exists** — concurrent cold logins were blowing the 30s budget as `Test timeout … exceeded while setting up storageState`. Warm-up failures are deliberately non-fatal so only the affected specs go red, attributably.
- **`getRecoveryLink(recipientEmail?)`** — the MailSlurper inbox is shared. An unfiltered subject match could open **another suite's** recovery mail and complete recovery against it, silently resetting that persona's harness credential for the rest of the run. `authentication-password-recovery.spec.ts` updated to pass its own address.

## Gates

- `tsc --noEmit` clean — `client-web` and `lib`
- `eslint` clean on every new/changed file
- Commit GPG-signed

## Run results — 15 / 16 green

Run against the local dev stack (client-web on `develop` incl. the merged #10176; Traefik origin `:3000`), `KRATOS_ADMIN_URL` set so `global-setup` provisions personas through the Kratos admin API.

| Run | Workers | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 15 passed, 1 failed (3.1m) |
| 2 | 2 | 15 passed, 1 failed (1.9m) |
| 3 | 1 | 15 passed, 1 failed (2.2m) |

The 15 are stable and fast (1.5-4.7s each) across all three runs — every case that exercises Connected Accounts itself is green.

### The one failure is NOT a test defect and NOT 051

**CA-41** times out at its first UI step, waiting for `Forgot password?`, with the login page frozen on *"Preparing secure sign-in…"*. Root cause reproduced with **zero test code involved** — a bare fresh browser context hitting `/login` directly:

```
401 /api/auth/oidc/id-token-hint | 302 /api/auth/oidc/login | 302 /oidc/login
303 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser
200 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser     <-- flow created TWICE
403 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/flows?id=...
{"error":{"id":"security_csrf_violation","code":403, ...}}
```

Two defects, both on the **login/OIDC bootstrap** — a surface 051 does not touch:

1. The login flow is created **twice** in one cold sign-in; the SPA then fetches the flow id from the URL while the anti-CSRF cookie has moved on, and Kratos rejects it with `security_csrf_violation`.
2. On that 403 the SPA **hangs indefinitely** on "Preparing secure sign-in…" — no error surfaced, no retry, no recovery.

Reproduction rate on this stack was high but not total (one fresh context in an early batch of three succeeded; a later batch of four failed 4/4), which is what made CA-41 look flaky before the cause was isolated.

This is the same *class* of bug the 051 review already fixed on the settings page ("settings flow created before `profileUrl` resolved — double flow creation, lost `return_to`"); this is the login page's version of it, and it is pre-existing.

**CA-41 is a regression guard for pre-existing recovery behaviour**, so it never reaches the 051 code under test. It should not gate this PR's assessment of the feature, but it does need a decision: fix the login bootstrap, or make CA-41 tolerate a stale flow id.

### Still manual

The 8 off-site OAuth round-trips (LinkedIn/Microsoft/GitHub) from the original walk stay out of automation; the provider hop is asserted up to the redirect only.

Runs the nightly `server-api` suite in parallel — **79.2 min → 44.5 min (~1.8×)**, measured on `test-alkem.io` — without weakening a single assertion. All 108 files still run; nothing is skipped,
  deleted or quarantined to gain speed.

  `workspace#040-parallel-nightly-server-api` · story #570

  ## How it works

  The 108-file `nightly` project becomes two projects in the **same** config, run as **one** invocation: `nightly-parallel` (94 files, `groupOrder: 0`, `maxWorkers` from `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS`) and
  `nightly-serial` (14 files, `groupOrder: 1`, `maxWorkers: 1`). Sequential groups give lane separation without a second config or a report merge. The legacy `nightly` project is left **byte-untouched**
  as the rollback surface — reverting is one line in `package.json`.

  Lane membership is **derived, never hand-maintained**: a guard applies hazard rules with name-scoped transitive taint, proves the two lanes partition the nightly scope exactly, and fails closed on
  drift. New spec files default to serial until proven safe — which is how two specs that arrived from `develop` mid-flight were classified with no manual step.

  Three mechanisms protect the signal: **serial-confirm** (any parallel failure is re-run at one worker, and the *serial* verdict is the job's exit code; parallel-fail/serial-pass is logged as
  interference and demotes a file after ≥2 in 7 nights), the **lane guard**, and a **retrospective baseline diff**.

  ## The main finding

  Four static-analysis passes added rules and demoted 22 files, and each run still found interference the rules missed. Two runs on identically fresh databases gave **7 and 63 failures** — same code, same
  data. Every one adjudicated as interference, never a real defect.

  The hazardous pattern is *"assert a shared pool user's privileged action succeeds"* — most of the suite, and not soundly detectable statically. The server compounds it: the `ActorContext` cache is keyed
  by actor alone and **deleted** on any credential change for that actor anywhere.

  So the sharing was removed. **Each vitest worker now gets its own 13 identities** (slot from `VITEST_POOL_ID`; worker 0 keeps bare addresses, worker N uses plus-addressing). Under `pool: 'threads'` a
  worker runs one file at a time, so two concurrently-executing files **cannot** resolve the same identity — structural, not heuristic. On `test-alkem.io` a full run then came back **`exit=0`, 108/108 
  files, 2003 passed, zero failures**.

  This needed a non-obvious fix: `GLOBAL_ADMIN` is granted by the server's bootstrap against the literal `admin@alkem.io`, so per-worker admins were unprivileged and every global-admin scenario failed
  `FORBIDDEN_POLICY`. The harness now grants platform roles per slot at startup using worker 0's bootstrap-privileged token.

  ## Teardown was silently broken

  `cleanUpBaseScenario` wrapped its whole delete sequence in **one** `try`, so the first failure skipped every delete after it. And `deleteOrganization` fails while the account still hosts anything — with
  the org **last**, that failure was invisible. An organisation leaked on essentially every run, of every suite using the factory.

  Measured: wall-clock rose **20.5 → 28.7 min across six consecutive runs**, then dropped straight back to 21.1 when the database was recreated. **~36% of runtime was accumulated residue** — larger than
  every optimisation here combined.

  Teardown is now per-entity best-effort and enumerates what the account still hosts, deleting in the required order (L2 → L1 → L0 → VCs → packs → org). Verified behaviourally: the organisation is
  genuinely gone afterwards, including when an untracked resource was created under its account.

  ## Also here

## What

Promotes the unified-collaboration e2e from an uncommitted debugging `.mjs` into the `test-suites` standard `functional-e2e` structure as a **committed, CI-gating** suite covering **both memo and whiteboard** (epic `003-unify-collab-yjs`, SC-009 / WS-F).

## Approach — service level (protocol/backend)

Two raw `y-websocket` clients per document open `ws://localhost:3000/collab/<id>?type=<memo|whiteboard>` carrying the admin OIDC/BFF session cookie on the handshake, exchanging Yjs sync + awareness. **No React/ProseMirror/Excalidraw UI.** The whiteboard test mirrors the `@alkemio/excalidraw-yjs-binding` Yjs scene schema (`elements`/`files`/`appState`, per-property nested `Y.Map`) **without importing it** — it tests the WS/CRDT layer, not the binding.

The OIDC/BFF login (one short-lived Playwright Chrome → `alkemio_session` cookie) is extracted into a reusable helper and shared by both specs.

## Scenarios & assertions

**Memo** (`memo-collaboration.spec.ts`):
- CRDT convergence A → B
- Awareness / presence
- Persistence round-trip *(opt-in, see below)*

**Whiteboard** (`whiteboard-collaboration.spec.ts`):
- Convergence A → B
- **Per-property merge (headline)** — A edits `element.x`, B edits the **same** element's `strokeColor` concurrently → **both survive on both clients, NOT last-write-wins**; untouched props intact
- Awareness / presence
- Persistence round-trip *(opt-in)*

## Files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `collab/collab-auth.ts` | OIDC/BFF admin login → cookie + cookie-authed GraphQL |
| `collab/collab-fixture.ts` | `createMemoFixture` / `createWhiteboardFixture` via GraphQL |
| `collab/collab-ws.ts` | raw-WS Yjs client + `waitForDoc` / `waitForAwareness` |
| `collab/memo-collaboration.spec.ts` | memo scenarios |
| `collab/whiteboard-collaboration.spec.ts` | whiteboard scenarios |
| `collab/README.md` | scenarios, headless-vs-live, run instructions |

## CI wiring

- New **`Collaboration`** project in `config/playwright.config.nightly.ts` (runs via `pnpm run test:nightly`).
- Adds `yjs` / `y-websocket` / `y-protocols` / `lib0` / `ws` (+ `@types/ws`) to `client-web` so `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` provides them in CI (lockfile updated).

## Proven headless now vs. live-only

Against the running local dev stack:
- ✅ **Deterministic / gating**: convergence, **per-property merge**, awareness — both memo and whiteboard. Default run: **2 passed / 2 skipped (18s)**.
- ⚠️ **Opt-in / non-gating**: the **persistence cold-rehydrate** assertions. The round-trip works intermittently but the cold client occasionally closes `1006` before the blob / `collaboration-fetch` flush completes, so enforcing it would flake CI. Skipped by default with a reason; run with `COLLAB_ASSERT_PERSISTENCE=true`. Enable once the persistence path is reliable.

## Requires (to execute)

The local dev stack must be up: gateway `localhost:3000` → unified collaboration service + server BFF (forward-auth + OIDC login). Tests scaffold fully and lint/typecheck without it; the live assertions need it.
